It was the name of a political formation in Croatia which was, according to our standards, very right-wing and very nationalistic. When the NDH was established in 1941, the Ustashas came to power and they implemented their nationalistic views, in particular against non-Croats in Croatia. And of course this term has very important historic connotations when it's being used 40 or 50 years after in the context that it was at the time in Croatia with the crisis there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which document specifically; the quotation at page 78 -- 77?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There's a document that's on the screen now for E-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. That's right. Right. But isn't that -- isn't that the same document as appears at page 77 of this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Your Honour. What appears in the report is reproductions of the most relevant passages from several documents, but in terms -- in order to give context and for completeness, I thought it would be appropriate to admit the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Will the document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 25, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll continue to the next document, which is 65 ter number 1240. The B/C/S ERN is 02077090 to 7091. And this is a letter by General Adzic, Mr. Theunens. Do you find that passage of your report? What -- while it's being brought up on E-court, what is said in this letter?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this letter dates from the 12th of October, 1991, and General Adzic, who is the Chief of the General Staff of the SFRY armed forces, states, among other things, that the role of the JNA is to defend parts of the Serbian people from genocide and biological extermination at the hands of Ustasha forces. Adzic also mentions in the letter, which is issued by the SSNO administration for moral guidance, that all armed units, JNA, TO, or volunteers, must act under the single command of the JNA. So we basically see a reiteration or repetition of the goals, JNA goals Kadijevic had mentioned in his letter of the 3rd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this also be admitted into evidence, this document that's on the E-court right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shall we give it an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 26, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, rather than go through them all individually, did you find other documents which supported this conclusion about a change in the JNA role?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. On page 80, there is a quotation from a directive on the use of the armed forces which was issued by Kadijevic on the 10th of December, 1991, which more or less repeats the same things we already discussed and also emphasises the importance of a single command over JNA, TO, and volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could interject there, could I ask that that be admitted into evidence without necessarily drawing it up on the E-court? I don't know if that procedure works but it would move things along a little faster in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think that position might be helpful. It's already admitted in terms of the report. Can we give it an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: For the Court officer's reference, it's 65 ter number 1277. The B/C/S ERN is 01061438 to 1442.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 27, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Proceed, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, were there any other documents on that issue that you'd like to highlight?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: On page 83, Your Honours, I quote -- in the middle of the page I quote from a report on the state of combat readiness of the 2nd Military District, which has 65 ter number 2047. Under the heading of the 9th Corps, the 9th JNA Corps was more or less deployed or covered more or less the area which is known as Northern Dalmatia in Croatia, so it is along the coast, with cities like Knin, east and west of Knin. There it mentions that the task consisted of protection of the population and features in-depth of its zone of responsibility. It is clear that the ethnic origin of the population is not specified in this section, but when we discuss orders from units subordinated to the 9th Corps that were issued during the time period covering early September to November 1991, we can better understand what is meant by the population, and we can actually conclude that it was only aimed at one part of the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you specify which pages of this document are most important, because it is more than ten pages long.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: For the English translation, it is page ERN 01109710, which is on the document page 12, under the heading of the 9th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this document also receive an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we please give the document an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 28, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, as the mission of the JNA changed, was that reflected in the ethnicity of the JNA members and officers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this particular aspect is not covered in this report, but when I drafted my report for the Milosevic case I had to look also at operations, for example, in Eastern Croatia and Baranja and also Western Slavonia and also analyse the evolution within various command bodies of the JNA, and from that analysis it became clear that in the course of fall 1991, all senior positions are occupied by officers of Serbian or Montegnegrin ethnicity, even though publicly they may have represented themselves as Yugoslavs. I have to add that officers -- or many officers of Slovene and Croatian ethnicity, in particular senior officers, left out of their own will or were removed, and there may also have been one officer of Slovene ethnicity, who was the deputy SSNO, so the deputy to Kadijevic, who stayed in his post. But when looking at operational groups elsewhere in Croatia, they were all commanded by officers of Serbian ethnicity during fall and winter 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm going to leave the subject of the JNA for the moment, and I'd like to focus your attention on changes in the Territorial Defence, or the TO. If you could look at pages 84 to 86 of your report - and pages 103 to 105 of the B/C/S - you discuss the emergence of ethnic Serb TOs during the year 1991. Could you just summarise what's included there, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we see that from January onwards in areas with a significant Serb ethnic presence, the TO which used to be a Republic of Croatia TO starts to split. Now, there are various reasons for that. In some areas the Croats say, "We don't want to cooperate with the JNA any more, or with the SFRY," and they create their own structures. In other areas, Croats are removed. In other areas, Serbs declare themselves, "We are now the TO of this municipality." But we see, to summarise that, a split of these republican TO, the Republic of Croatia, into call it ethnically pure structures whereby - and that's the subject of my report - local Serbs in a number of areas established their own TO structures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mention -- do you specify those areas in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. On the top of page 85, some examples are listed of areas in Croatia where Serbs created their own Territorial Defence, and the supporting materials are then mentioned in the footnotes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to have you -- I'd like to call up on E-court one particular document. It's 65 ter number 56. The B/C/S ERN is 02172109 to 2109. And this is the document, Mr. Theunens, which is referred to on page 84 of your report, and I'd just like you, in one or two sentences, to summarise what that document says and why it's important, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is an order signed by Dr. Milan Babic, President of the Executive Board of the SAO Krajina, so the Serb Autonomous District Krajina, to, I assume, municipalities located on the territory controlled by the Executive Board of the SAO Krajina to mobilise the TO, and also mobilise volunteer units. I would wish to add that in the conclusion, Milan Babic requests the government of the Republic of Serbia for assistance. And this seems pretty obvious, because of course these structures are not answering to Croatia any more, so they have to find another authority, not just to receive orders from, that's not the issue here, but to provide assistance, be it in manpower or know-how or in logistical assistance in order to establish these own TO structures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we raise the conclusion on the monitor up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could perhaps zoom in -- if the usher could zoom in on the part of the document in English that says "Conclusion" so that the Trial Chamber can read that, please. Your Honour, I think this is our first attempt at zooming in, so if it takes a moment, please bear with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just remind us, what are SUPs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, SUP refers -- means actually secretariat for the interior. Now, I don't know the B/C/S acronym, the B/C/S equation by heart, but it's included in the glossary at the end of the report. It means that the Republic of Serbia is requested to provide technical support to the secretariats, or call it police offices, of the Serbian Autonomous Region -- excuse me, Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Secretariat of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed MUP is on the ministerial level and SUP is on the local level, secretariat level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this document receive an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will the document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 29, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At page 86 of the report, Mr. Theunens - page 105 in B/C/S - you refer to some problems faced by the Territorial Defence in Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And if I could ask that 65 ter number 1851 be put on the screen, please. The B/C/S ERN for this document is 02807753 to 7754.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you have a hard copy in front of you, I'll go ahead and -- here, now it's on the screen. Could you please just tell us what is of significance in this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is -- we could call it a status report, dated 25th of November, 1991, and signed by - that's only visible on the last page - the command of the municipal TO staff in Benkovac. Benkovac is a municipality west of Knin on the territory of the entity known as the SAO Krajina. Now, on the second -- I would like to go to the second page of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we have it now. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, when you look on the monitor, on the seventh line, so just under the part that is underlined, it mentions one of the problems TO units or local Serb or SAO Krajina TO units are facing, that is that due to mobilisation by the JNA, there is a lack of manpower. If you -- if we go a bit further now, it's actually the last line that is currently visible, yes, now the top. It says, "The structure of the TO and the system of RiK was initially dependent own the RiK signals system of the police units." RiK is the B/C/S acronym or abbreviation for command and control. It means that the TO had to rely not only on the structure established already by the SAO Krajina Police, but also on the equipment, because there is mention of a signals system. The existence of such a system means that not only a commander can issue orders to subordinates, be it TO or police, but this commander can also receive information from subordinate units, be it police or TO. I would like to go then to the third page of the document, where we could -- we could zoom on the bottom half. Okay. There the report mentions the existence of what is -- excuse me, what is described as considerable presence of crime at all levels. It also talks about problems at the political level, both local as well as at the level of the SAO Krajina. And according to the -- to the author of the report, this -- I mean, the nature of the political situation has had a negative impact on the population and the members of the TO. The last item I would like to mention in this paragraph is the comment by the author where he says - and that's the last sentence of this paragraph - "Because the legal system is not functioning, there is reason to fear of the above -" i.e., the problems I just discussed - "and also the creation of many political and private paramilitary formations." One can assume that the author focus -- addresses here illegal paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence and given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May we please give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 30, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, moving on, you stated earlier in your testimony that the SFRY armed forces consisted of the JNA and the TO. Did the SAO Krajina ever define its armed forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. The SAO Krajina and subsequently the RSK defined its armed forces at different stages, and these are enumerated in the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I can focus your attention first at page 87, and ask that document with the 65 ter number 105 be placed on E-court, please. This is at page 107 in the B/C/S, by the way. Mr. Theunens, I believe you have a hard copy in front of you, and also the most relevant parts are reproduced in your report at page 87. Could you just mention what is significant about this decision.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the context of this report, the Articles 1, 5, and 6 are the most relevant. Article 1 we addressed already earlier during my testimony. It mentions that the law of defence of the Republic of Serbia will be applied on the territory of the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina. Article 5, which is at the bottom of the page, I think, Article 5 establishes the armed forces of the SAO Krajina. Two components: Territorial Defence and then units known as Special Purpose Units of the Krajina Ministry of Interior. Article 6, which is on the second page of the decision, at the top, states: "The President of the Government of the SAO Krajina is by his position commander of the Territorial Defence"; i.e., armed forces of the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina. Now, I would wish to add I'm not a legal expert, but it's interesting that whereas in Article 5 the Special Purpose Unit of the Krajina Ministry of Interior are mentioned as one of the components of the armed forces of the SAO Krajina, in Article 6, Article 6 seems to suggest that the president is only the commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this receive an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we please give the document an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 31, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, there was -- you mentioned the reference to the Special Purpose Units of the Krajina Ministry of the Interior. Can you explain who that was? Can you clarify who that refers to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this refers to Special Purpose police units, actually. I will rephrase it. I apologise. In military terms, Special Purpose Units are often called special forces. So these are highly trained, specialised units which carry out particular -- let's call them sensitive operations. They're highly mobile, they have the best training, best equipment. They can be used, in current situations, for anti-terrorism operation, to extract hostages, and so on. Now, we know that the SAO Krajina, on the 29th of May, established Special Purpose Units of the Ministry of Interior, and this is explained in my report on the top of page 90.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps -- I apologise for the interruption, but we could just pull up 65 ter number 78. The B/C/S ERN is 02141921. And that's a 29 May 1991 decision. Mr. Theunens, can you see that document in front of you? Please continue with your explanation.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: So this document, which is a decision signed by the president of the Assembly of the SAO Krajina, states in Article 1 - if we move a bit further on the page - thank you - that Special Purpose Units of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina, Ministry of Interior, will be formed and they will be called Krajina police, and they will be under the authority of the Ministry of Defence, which is quite interesting, because on the one hand it says they are Ministry of Interior, but subordination is then clarified, and it says "Ministry of Defence." In Article 2, which is further detailed on the second page, the duties of these Special Purpose Units of the Ministry of Interior are specified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'd ask that this receive an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will the document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 32, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, who was the SAO Krajina Minister of the Interior in 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: For the largest part of 1991, Milan Martic was minister of interior of the entity known as the SAO Krajina. However, during a certain time period covering from 29th of May, 1991, onwards, and I was not able to establish a clear end date, Milan Martic was also minister of defence of the entity known as the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say "also," you mean he held two posts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on the documents I've seen, these documents indeed suggest that he held both posts. Now, I mentioned that I don't -- I was not able to determine an exact end date for him holding the post of minister of defence. I've seen an order afterwards, but it's not included in my report, where in November 1991 a Mr. Tarbuk is appointed to the position of minister of defence. I think this is the end of November 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I ask you to look at a couple of documents that may help give some specificity to this. The first one is 65 ter number 45. The B/C/S ERN is 02172060. If that could be placed on the screen, please. What does this document say?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This document is an order appointing Milan Martic to the position of secretary of internal affairs of SAO Krajina, and it's signed by Milan Babic, chairman of the Executive Council. It is dated the 4th of January, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- the phrase used here is "Secretary for Internal Affairs." How does that compare or relate to minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on my understanding, the secretary for internal affairs and his secretariat are the same bodies as ministries but at that stage the terminology was "secretary" and "secretariat," and later on that terminology was changed into "ministry" and "minister."

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could admit this document, then we'll move on to another one that may help with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we please give the document an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will Exhibit Number 33, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next document is 65 ter number 91, the B/C/S ERN being 02141944.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you now explain what this document is.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This document, Your Honours, is a decision by the Assembly of the SAO Krajina, signed by the president, to elect Milan Martic to the position of minister of interior of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I apologise. It was the 27th of June, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I would ask that this receive an exhibit number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document please be given an exhibit number and admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 34, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: By the way, Your Honour, in terms of vocabulary, sometimes I ask for an exhibit number, sometimes I say to be admitted into evidence. I do intend to request that all of these be admitted into evidence and not merely marked for identification. I hope that's been clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Black, for clarifying that point. All documents admitted so far and given exhibit numbers, may be -- may they please be also admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document I'd like you to look at, Mr. Theunens, is 65 ter number 79. The B/C/S ERN of this document is 02141844.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise for the fact that we are not following the chronological order, because this order -- this document is dated 29th of May, 1991, and it actually refers to what I mentioned earlier, the appointment, again by the Assembly of the SAO Krajina, of Milan Martic to the position of minister of defence of the SAO Krajina. So when we go -- summarise the two previous exhibits we saw, we had one for an appointment to secretary in January, then we had one for an appointment to minister of interior in June, if I'm not wrong. This one is dated 29th of May, so indeed it would suggest that Milan Martic had held both positions, minister of interior and minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does it mean that or does it mean that he was appointed minister of defence on the 29th of May, 1991, and minister of interior in June, 1991? We don't know when he was appointed minister of interior in June he was stripped of his Ministry of Defence. We still need that to be confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to add, in relation to this document, it's dated 29th of May, 1991, and it is the same date of the document we discussed earlier that established the Special Purpose Units of the SAO Krajina Ministry of Interior, which were to be subordinated to the Ministry of Defence. From an analytical point of view, one would be tempted to make a link between both documents and to conclude that because Milan Martic is minister of defence, the Special Purpose Units of the Ministry of Interior are also subordinated to the Ministry of Defence at that time. And in the report it is explained -- in my report it is explained that the subordination of the Special Purpose Units changes, and that in the -- at the latest in the course of August they are subordinated to the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was there any change in the Ministry of Defence in August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on the documents I saw, there was no change, but there may well have been a document but we don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before we get away from this document, could it please be exhibited and admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 35, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to look at another exhibit now -- or another document. 65 ter number 2051, B/C/S ERN 03639723 to 9742. Mr. Theunens, if you see that document in front of you, could you please tell me -- well, does this document address the duties of the ministers of interior and of defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, these duties are addressed in this document. We have to take into account that the document dates from the 2nd of December, 1991. So it's fairly late. In looking at the events that are relevant for this report, it is fairly late.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which portions of this document are relevant to us, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the -- for the purposes of this report, I would like to draw your attention to Article 9, which lists the responsibilities of the minister of defence. And again I would like to emphasise that the document dates from December 1991, which is fairly late. And then also under title 5, Territorial Defence, there is the Article 31, and following Articles, 32, 33, and 35, which address issues related to the Territorial Defence and the command of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could those receive a number and be admitted into evidence, please? Could that document, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 36, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you've looked at some documents and explained to us about Mr. Martic holding some positions in the Interior Ministry and of Defence. Did he hold any other positions in the SAO Krajina government, please? In 1991.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, within the government, based on the documents I saw, Mr. Martic did not hold other positions. However, there is an 8th of August, 1991, decision by Milan Babic, which is discussed on page 91 in my report, according to which Milan Martic is appointed deputy commander of the Territorial Defence of the SAO Krajina. And this decision is mentioned in 65 ter number 112.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Theunens. You're anticipating my next question there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may not be necessary even to draw that up if -- to bring it up on the E-court since he's already addressed its significance. If it could be given a number and admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given a number, exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 37, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, the Chamber asked you a question which gets to this same point, but I would like to try to make sure that it's as clear as it can be. We saw a reference to the special police units being subordinated to the minister of defence, but then we also see a reference to the minister of the interior. Based on your analysis, who commanded the special police units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, my report focuses on Territorial Defence, and I didn't study police issues as such. However, when I came -- I came across documents dealing with police issues, and from those documents except one that stated that the special police units were subordinated to the Ministry of Defence, so from the documents I came across, the special purpose police units were subordinated to the Ministry of Interior; i.e., Milan Martic. But I understand that there will be another witness who will speak about that issue in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The special purpose police that you say were subordinated to the Ministry of Interior, are those -- do they go by another name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes the name -- in open sources you would see the name of Marticevci, for example, Martic police, Krajina police, but again I would like to refer Your Honour to the other witness who will testify about that because it's actually outside my field of expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And if I could add, because maybe I mis-expressed myself a bit when I was talking about the subordination of the special police units, that during a certain time period they were indeed subordinated to the Ministry of Defence, as we've seen in the documents, and that was when Mr. Martic was minister of defence. And then in -- at the latest in August, they become subordinated to the Ministry of Interior. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In August, what was Mr. Martic's post? Was he minister of interior or minister of defence or minister of both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was certainly minister of interior. Minister of defence, I would assume yes, but -- actually I cannot give an answer. I would prefer not to give an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, who was the ultimate commander-in-chief of the SAO Krajina armed forces, according to your analysis?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: According to the documents we have discussed, it would be the president of the government of the SAO Krajina; i.e., Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you know this, but if you do, do you know the dates of his Presidency, when he was the president of the SAO Krajina, Milan Babic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: He was the president during the whole time -- I mean, when we look at 1991, he started as the secretary of the government, I think, in the early days when there was still secretaries, and then he became president of the government and he stayed in that position until early 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you some questions about the relationship between Milan Martic, the accused, and Milan Babic. First of all, could you explain the de jure situation between the two of them and their positions.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't make a political analysis, but still based on the documents I reviewed, and the texts are straightforward, Milan Babic, as the president of the government, he is the commander or is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces, and -- which means that the armed forces consisting of Territorial Defence and police ultimately answer to him. Now, we discussed this one -- the 1st of August decision on the composition of the armed forces. There it was indicated that the president was in command of the Territorial Defence; i.e., the armed forces, but the second component of the armed forces was not mentioned. Now, I'm not in a position to draw any conclusions on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was the definition of the armed forces not given at any stage somewhere during the period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in fact there were many definitions, but they were not always coherent. And there are -- when you look at the situation as in August, there are decisions are taken August, September, decisions are taken on a daily basis, and it's as if somebody wants to enforce his authority; i.e., the person issuing all these decisions. And these decisions are not always, from my point of view, from the military point of view, they are not always coherent. So indeed the armed forces are at one stage defined as the Territorial Defence and the Special Purpose Units of the Ministry of Interior subordinated at that stage - i.e., on the 29th of May - to the Ministry of Defence, but then there is the 1st of August decision where it is clearly stated that the president of the government - i.e., Babic - is in command of the armed forces but only the TO is mentioned. Now, is it just an omission or does it mean more? I assume that Milan Babic is the best person to talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to launch into several documents which may in fact clarify some of these issues. Perhaps it's an appropriate time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe before you even launch into those documents, if I may just ask -- make a request. If it is at all possible, if it is possible sometime during your testimony, if you could maybe give us a bar chart showing the periods during which, according to the information at your disposal, Mr. Martic held the various positions covering the period 1990 to 1995. And if it's not possible, please just say it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is -- it is possible, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. You don't have to say -- tell us whether he held two positions simultaneously, but just give the dates. We'll see where the overlap is. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes. You did say it was a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will take a break now. We'll come back at 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I resume, Mr. Theunens, you did an excellent job of slowing down during the last session. I'm going to try to follow your example, and if we could continue that comfortable pace, please do so. Just before the break, you had talked a little bit about the de jure situation, the relationship between Mr. Martic and Mr. Babic. I'm going to show you some documents, and I'm going to ask you to focus on the de facto relationship between those two men. For those following along and, Mr. Theunens, for you as well, this is covered in pages 96 to 99 of the report. I apologise, I don't have the B/C/S corresponding pages but I think that will become apparent. The first document is 65 ter number 109. The B/C/S ERN is 02076701. If that could be brought up, please. Mr. Theunens, for hard copies, if you're looking there, this is a report dated 6 August, 1991. There it is. Now, what I'd like you to do for this document and those that follow, if you'd please look at it, tell us what it is, and explains its significance for this case.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a report which actually includes an order by Milan Martic. The order can be found at the bottom of the first page, and it says that "due to the visit of the SFRY vice-president, Branko Kostic, and a peace delegation, Milan Martic has issued an order for a cease-fire ..." On the second page there is information on the operational situation, which is at the moment of less interest. I would also like to draw your attention, again on the first page, to the list of addressees, where it says "To Supreme Commander SAO Krajina TO." One would assume that this is Milan Babic, based on the de jure documents -- on the documents we have seen describing the de jure situation. The "Secretary of the SAO Krajina SUP" refers to Milan Martic. ODB, state security department, there I have no name. Commander of the TO I have no name either, but then the next name is a person described as Frenki. Now, based on other documents, and they are also included in the report, Frenki is the nickname for a person called Franko Simatovic, who has been indicted by the ICTY, and who at the time of the events was a senior official in the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. It is noteworthy that an official of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia is among the addressees of a report providing operational information on the situation in the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be given a number and admitted into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 38, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Just for my edification, you said, Mr. Theunens, it is noteworthy that among the addressees is who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An individual described here, identified as Frenki.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who was at that time a senior official in the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. And normally, at least in the military context, reports discussing operational issues are only sent to persons who have a need to know, to assess them in their decision-making or for other need-to-know purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Unless the Chamber has further questions, perhaps we could pull up the next document, which is 65 ter number 1941. The B/C/S ERN is 02806536 to 6537.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, again what is this document and what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a similar document as the one we just discussed. Whereas the previous one discussed the time period 5, 6 August, this report we're looking at now discusses the situation for the 18th and 19th of July, 1991. Milan Martic is again one of the addressees, secretary of SUP, so Ministry of Interior, that's Milan Martic. And Frenki is again identified by his nickname. And in the report, operational developments covering both the Ministry of Interior forces as well as the TO are being discussed, with the focus there on TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document also receive a number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. The document is admitted into evidence and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 39, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document that I'll ask the witness to look at is 65 ter number 144. The B/C/S ERN is 01075267 to 5768.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a document, as you can see from the heading in the left top corner, a document issued by the SAO Krajina TO Main Staff, or the command, in simple terms, of the SAO Krajina TO, dated 17th of September, 1991. It is sent to the Supreme Commander of the SAO Krajina armed forces, which will be the civilian authority, the commander of the SAO Krajina armed forces, the TO chief, and the state security. And the most important aspect of this document can be found, if you go a bit to the bottom - stop - we see a line there: "At 1750, Secretary Milan Martic issued the following order." There are four points which follow, and these concern forces or elements of the TO. So this document indicates that Milan Martic, as secretary of the interior of the SAO Krajina, was in the position to issue orders to forces of the SAO Krajina TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be given a number and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, and may it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 40, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 211. The B/C/S ERN is 02077593 to 7602. Mr. Theunens, could you tell us what this document is and what significance it has.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document requests -- excuse me, describes or includes a number of requests for ammunition and other military equipment for, as you can see from the document, various TO units. It starts with the Knin TO, but further on in the document other units of the TO of the SAO Krajina are mentioned. And on the last page -- if we could show the last page. Yeah, it should actually be two pages back, then, ERN 0301, in the English, 9264. Obviously on the English translation there is no signature, but on the B/C/S version, on page 02077601, we see the signature of Milan Martic, where he signs as minister. If we go back now to the first page of the document, we can see the addressees. So this request is addressed to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia, and more specifically to Tomislav Simovic, who was at that time minister of defence. The fact that it mentions personally in military terms means that it's an important document, because otherwise it would have been sufficient to just send it to the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does this document tell us about the de facto power of Mr. Martic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It shows that Milan Martic, we know that -- we know for sure that he's minister of interior. He may still be minister of defence. He may also still be deputy commander of the TO. But it shows that he is in a position to send requests to the Republic of Serbia for significant amounts of military equipment. We don't need to go through all the -- through the entire document, but when we look on the first page and we look at the requirements for the Knin TO, we see, for example, in item 8, that 630.000 rounds of 7.9 millimetre heavy charge bullets are being requested. And again line 5, we see 1 million rounds of a particular calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could this be given a number and admitted, please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 41, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document on the same general topic is 65 ter number 166. The ERN in B/C/S is 02077929. Mr. Theunens, could you please discuss this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is an order issued by Milan Babic, who signs as Prime Minister, dated 9th of October, 1991, and it addresses an issue Your Honours actually mentioned earlier, the relationship between police and Territorial Defence during operations. In this order, Milan Babic states that during the preparation and the execution of combat tasks, all police units in the territory of the SAO Krajina have to be subordinated or actually are subordinated to the territorial -- to the competent Territorial Defence officer. At the bottom of the order you see that Milan Martic -- excuse me, Milan Babic makes reference to an Article of the 1982 Law on All People's Defence of the SFRY, an article which is also quoted in the beginning of my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, does this suggest to us or tell to us about the relationship between Milan Babic and Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: At least, Your Honours, it shows that Milan Babic, he makes an attempt to subordinate the TO -- excuse me, to subordinate the police to the TO. Now, whether he has to issue an order for that or it would have -- you would have expected the Ministry of Interior; i.e., Milan Martic, to issue such an order, that is -- that is an open question, but at least it shows that Milan Babic tries to impose his authority over the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be given a number and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 42, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 1256. The B/C/S ERN is 02011636. Mr. Theunens, please give us your comments on this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This document, Your Honours, is sent by the commander of the 2nd Lika Brigade, a Colonel Petar Trbovic, who in the first part of the document mentions that he has been sent, together with a group of officers, by the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence. The 2nd Lika Brigade could be a TO unit or a JNA unit. When I say "TO," it means SAO Krajina TO. The document is a request to Milan Martic, identified as "Comrade Martic," to use his influence to remove a group led by an individual called Predrag Bakalic, because this group has not behaved according to the required standards during operations. I would also like to draw your attention to the third paragraph, where it is mentioned that Predrag Bakalic is a captain who commands a group of specially trained persons trained in Golubic, and Golubic is the training centre I mentioned earlier where, according to documents I reviewed - and these documents are included in the report - members or future members of these Special Purpose Units of the SAO Krajina Police were trained with the assistance of an individual called or named Captain Dragan, Dragan Vasiljkovic, and also officials of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. And the police witness who will testify later will provide more details on Predrag Bakalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be given a number and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 43, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last document on this particular topic is 65 ter number 1217, and the B/C/S ERN is 02170999. And this one, I apologise, Mr. Theunens, I put it slightly out of chronological order, but when it comes up on the screen if you could tell us what it is and comment upon its significance.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an intelligence report compiled by the state security service of the SAO Krajina. It is -- it's a quite early document - 11th of June, 1991 - and it specifies a number of issues that are related by what I described as power struggle between Martic and -- between Mr. Martic and Mr. Babic in my report starting on page 95 in the English version. Where we see in the beginning of the document "Political complex," as it has been translated, it mentions a disagreement between Babic and Martic over the appointment of new SAO Krajina ministers, in particular minister of internal affairs. Further on when we look under the second heading, "Military complex," which is a bit lower on that page, it says that SAO Krajina special forces made a show of force in Grahovo and Drvar, and then it says this is Martic's premature improvisation now. Martic, the R has been forgotten, because when we look in the B/C/S copy, ERN 02170999, it clearly states Marticevoj, so it talks about Milan Martic. And again from the context one can conclude that there is not only a kind of a power struggle between Martic and Babic but also that Martic has -- is in a position of authority over SAO Krajina special forces. The second page, finally, mentions - the third bullet - "the Knin Corps of the JNA -" which is also known under the name 9th Corps - "allowed us -" and that's probably the SAO Krajina Territorial Defence - "to take a certain amount of heavy weaponry from their depots," which refers to an issue of support that the JNA units provided to the SAO Krajina TO, which is discussed more extensively further on in the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could just interrupt you for a moment. That paragraph, it talks about weapons originally intended for the TO, but you said you thought "us" was the TO. Who do you think "us" refers to, "allowed us to take a certain amount of weapons"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I agree that there is room for interpretation, but I would assume -- I mean, there are actually two options. Based on the nature of the weapons, I would assume that these are weapons which may have belonged to the TO of the Republic of Croatia, because we know that they have been confiscated in May 1990, and then handed over to the SAO Krajina TO. However, we also know that the special police forces had military equipment. And again, special police forces of the SAO Krajina are not addressed in detail in my report, but I -- I agree that there is room for interpretation here, that it could well be that with "us" it is meant SAO Krajina Police units or special police units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning, talking about this document, you mentioned that it was authored by the state security service.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which ministry does the state security service pertain to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: State security is subordinated to the Ministry of Interior. And again, the police witness will talk about that in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So just -- just so it's clear, this document was written by someone who was part of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could this document be given a number and be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The number that -- the document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 44, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we've been discussing civilian authority over the TO for the most part during 1991 and perhaps on into 1992. I'd like to shift focus slightly and focus now on the military command over the TO during that same time. You addressed this starting at page 102 of your report, which is page 122 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. In this section, military command and control, two important aspects are discussed. First of all, the SAO Krajina TO staff; and secondly, command and control during operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just -- well, let's take those one at a time. Could you very briefly summarise what's said about the SAO Krajina staff -- TO staff, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Milan Babic - and that's the top of page 103 - on 30th of September appointed a JNA officer, a retired JNA officer, Ilija Djuric, to the position of command of the SAO Krajina TO. He was relieved of his duties on the 20th of November, 1991, and replaced by Colonel Radoslav Maksic, who was also a JNA officer. And then to conclude, on the 10th of October, Milan Babic sent a report on the status of the TO of the SAO Krajina, confirming actually that the staff had been formed through the Chief of General Staff of the SFRY armed forces, General Blagoje Adzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just briefly, what's the content of that? Is anything requested in that report by President Babic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I would have to see the actual document, because I didn't quote in my report. Indeed, he requests assistance, as I mentioned in my report, but I haven't specified the request for assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Let's focus now on the second element that you mentioned, which is command and control during combat operations. So first if you could just give us a quick summary. What was the command and control arrangement between the JNA and the Serb TO during operations in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on the documents I looked at, the command relation was as such that efforts were made to apply the principles of command and control, and that means that, according to the documents I looked at, that the TO of the SAO Krajina units that were involved in operations together with the JNA were subordinated to JNA officers. In some areas operational groups and tactical groups were created; in other areas, not. In addition, there is also information about subordination of SAO Krajina Police units to JNA units in certain areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning to page 106, and actually between pages 106 and 112 of your report, which are pages 127 to 133 of the B/C/S version, you give a number of examples of unified command over JNA and local Serb forces in areas of relevance to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it helps you follow along, I note that there's a map at page 104 of the report - page 125 - on the colour copies that I distributed that may help. I pinpoint these locations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm going to show you a number of documents, and as we've been doing, for each one if you could identify the author, the date, who it's to, and then give us an idea of why it's relevant. The first one is 65 ter number 699. The B/C/S ERN is 00847711 to 7761. And it's a fairly lengthy document, but the relevant passages, I think to help direct the usher, would be 00913548 in English, and 00847750 -- 50 in B/C/S. Maybe while we're there on the first page, Mr. Theunens, if you could just identify this document, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, this is, as the title mentions, are the minutes of the 16th session of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 12th of May, 1992, in Banja Luka. This Assembly is part of the self-declared Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which became later known as the RS, Republika Srpska. And here it gives -- this document provides the minutes of the discussions that were -- that took place during this Assembly session. Of interest for us is the page mentioned by Mr. Black. If we could go to that page, which is 00913548.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Black, what page is that in normal language?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think on the E-court, here on this one it actually shows indeed the ERNs, so ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed. And if we could go to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And that's page 48 of the document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I was looking at the hard copy earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this page is an extract from the speech General Ratko Mladic gave during the Assembly session. When he was still a colonel, Ratko Mladic was the chief of staff of the 9th JNA Corps in Knin, and then in the beginning of 1992 he was transferred to Bosnia-Herzegovina, where in May 1992 he took up command of the self-declared VRS, or the armed forces of the Bosnian Serbs. In this section, Mladic directly addresses Milan Martic, who is among the attendees, and states and talks about the situation in Kijevo. Kijevo was a small town just south-east of Knin, and Kijevo was taken over by the JNA and forces of the Ministry of Interior, so police forces of the SAO Krajina, on the 26th of August, 1991. And in this extract, Ratko Mladic explains how this was done. He says to Martic: "Well, look, I asked you for 40 policemen." These 40 policemen were provided. And he -- actually, the most important aspect of that is the sentence before, where Mladic says that: "The Knin Corps was successful because under a single command in the zone of the corps -" 9th Corps - "were the JNA, Territorial Defence forces, and Martic's Police ..." Now, I would like to add a bit -- brief lines about Kijevo. When you look on the map at page 104, the territory covered by the SAO Krajina is not indicated as such on the map, but it is important to know that certainly in -- at the day -- at the date of these events in June 1991, there is no territorial integrity of the SAO Krajina, nor is there a homogenous ethnic make-up. There are villages, there are locations within the territory claimed as the SAO Krajina where non-Serbs are living. And Slunj, for example, which you can find on the map on page 104 just below the word Kordun, so Slunj located in Lika, had, according to the 1991 census figures, which can be found in the atlas, an absolute majority of Croats. There were other municipalities with -- with significant presences, most of the times minorities but significant presences of non-Serbs in the territory that was claimed as being part of the SAO Krajina. The reason why Kijevo was taken over was according to a warning Milan Martic had sent to the Croatian police in Split, and this warning is mentioned on page 106 in my report, that -- and I will quote now from this document -- it's only mentioned in my report on page 106. Martic says: "We will not allow your police stations, upholders and guardians of the Ustasha and fascist policy of the so-called Young Croatian Democracy anywhere in the SAO Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we get away from this document, I neglected to ask that 65 ter number 699, the minutes that are on your screen, could those be given a number and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The document is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 45, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 2054, 2054. And the B/C/S ERN is 04143802.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an order by the commander of the 221st Motorised Brigade, a JNA unit which was subordinated to the 9th Corps, Colonel Borislav Djukic, dated 9th of October, 1991. I should make a correction: It's not an order, it's a combat report. So it starts with description of the operational -- the recent operational developments. Of interest for us at this stage is the top of page 2, where Colonel Borislav Djukic makes a number of requests. He requests joint planning of activities towards Skradin, which is in the vicinity of Drnis - that is south-east of Knin - and he suggests coordinated action with the SAO Krajina JTO -- actually, he refers to Jedinice [phoen] TO units, and Krajina SUP, so Krajina police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this receive a number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 46, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 2055. The B/C/S ERN is 04143825. This is another document from Colonel Djukic. Mr. Theunens, could you please address this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I can be brief Your Honours. The paragraph of interest in this context is the second paragraph, paragraph which starts on the second page. So it's heading number 2. And when we zoom in on the proposal that Colonel Djukic makes, he makes a proposal in relation to mobilisation of SAO Krajina TO forces, and he also mentioned that a tank platoon of T-34s - so a JNA unit - was subordinated to the 1st Brigade of the TO. So this document shows that there is close cooperation, and this includes, of course, what we mentioned earlier, the subordination of the TO to the JNA. And in this particular situation that elements of the JNA can be subordinated also to TO units, again, just to maintain single command during operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this receive a number, please, and be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 47, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more document with regard to Drnis. This is 65 ter number 2065. The B/C/S ERN is 04143860.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think they've hopefully caught me out in a slip of dyslexia. This is 65 ter number 2056, not 2065. I think I misspoke, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what we see in front of us, I believe, is the B/C/S version. Okay. Now we have the English. Could you please comment on this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This is a report from the commander of the Tactical Group number 1, dated 16 of November 1991, to the commander of the 9th Corps of the JNA. At the end of the document, on the second page, it mentions among the casualties -- back to the top, please. It's on the fourth or the fifth line in the document. It mentions among the casualties military reserve corporal, so a soldier from the 221st Motorised Brigade as well as Dragan Milic, a member of the SAO Krajina Ministry of Interior. So this indicates that in Tactical Group number 1 there was also at least one member of the SAO Krajina Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could that document also be given a number and admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 48, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document I'd like to look at is 65 ter number 1857. The B/C/S ERN is 01134461 to 4468. Mr. Theunens, first, what locality is -- is at issue in this document for our purposes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It talks about an attack on the city of Sibenik, which -- I don't have the map in front of me but if I recall well, it's located west of Knin, on the coast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it south-west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's south-west, Your Honour. Thank you. It's located on the coast, and this is an order issued by the commander of the 9th JNA Corps. Military orders -- and this always follow the same template. At least, orders for operations, they follow the same template. There will be first a discussion, paragraph 1, about the enemy. Then there will also be a discussion what neighbouring units are doing. Here when we go through the document, on the bottom of page 3, heading 4, "I decided ..." that is the most important part because there the commander will issue the orders to his subordinate units, and he will explain for each of his subordinate unit what they will do. In paragraph 4, or in heading 4, he gives the general mission, and in heading 5 he will specify that mission for the specific subordinate units he has.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, sorry, just to interrupt for a moment so we can catch up in scrolling down. Are you -- okay. Now can you see the heading 4 that you were just referring to there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, I see the heading 4. I apologise for going too fast. So heading 4, the commander gives the mission. In -- the mission he actually received from his superior commander. And then in heading 5, when we scroll further --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that actually on the next page?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It's on the next page. Sorry. It's on the bottom of the next page -- excuse me. It starts on -- in the middle of the next page. Yeah, we jumped a bit, but we can go back a page, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we go backwards one page? I think we skipped a page. Is that the right page, Mr. Theunens, or one more?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: One more. We need the heading 5. Yes. So in the heading 5, the commander gives the specific mission of each of his subordinate units, and these are then listed in the subparagraphs 5.1, 5.2, and so on. Of interest for us is then the subparagraph 5.6, which can be found at the bottom of the next page. Yes. At the bottom of the screen we can see now "TO staff SAO Krajina." So the commander of the 9th Corps also issues orders to the TO staff of the SAO Krajina. And this continues on -- also on the next page into the subparagraph 5.7, which is a bit lower. Yes. Where the commander of the 9th Corps also issues orders to what is identified as security forces of the SAO. Now, from the military point of view, based on the fact that he talks about TO and he identifies it as TO, security forces can only be police forces. Now, it's not clear from the order whether he's talking about the special forces of the police or the regular, if we can call it regular, SAO Krajina Police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What would be the significance of that difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in my view it would not be significant, because at that stage, at the 31st of October, based on the documents we've seen earlier, then the special forces of the police and the police as such are all subordinated to the Ministry of Interior. So from the subordination point of view, there is no -- it has no real advantages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so it's clear, who was the minister of interior at that time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: At that time, Milan Martic was the minister of interior, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this receive a number and be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. Would you please give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 49, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continuing with this same theme of examples of unified command, the next document is 65 ter number 1247. The B/C/S ERN, I believe, is 02009444 to 9445. Mr. Theunens, could you please tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an order from the 5th Military District. We didn't go into details in relation to military districts when we were discussing the structure of the JNA, but basically the territory of the Republic of Croatia was covered by two -- by three military districts: The 5th, which covered Slovenia, Western Croatia; the 1st Military District which covered the largest part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Eastern Croatia and Western Serbia; and the Naval Military District, which covered the coastal areas. So this is the 5th Military District. An order is issued for the forming of a Tactical Group 2. Now, the numbering of the tactical groups has nothing to do with the area where they are active. I mention that because there may well be a Tactical Group 2 active in other areas at the same time, but these are just temporary formations which were only established for specific operations and which will only exist during a specific time period, and once the mission has been accomplished or the commander decides that there is no further requirement for a tactical group or operational group, then they are disbanded. Of interest here is paragraph 3, so the heading number 3, where it says: "The task of Tactical Group 2 is to unite the activities of the JNA units at the artillery range in Slunj and the TO units in Veljun and Plaski ..." Veljun and Plaski are located -- Plaski is located south-west of Slunj - it's not visible on the map - but these are obviously units of the SAO Krajina TO, and it shows again the attempts or the desire to impose a single and unified command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document please receive a number and be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given a number, exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 50, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 1257. The B/C/S ERN is 01099990 to 9995.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, again this is an order for operations. In order to identify the unit that has issued the order, we need to go to the last page. We need to go to page 5 of six pages, so page 5, where it says commander Colonel Cedomir Bulat, who was a JNA officer and in command of a JNA, I believe a brigade, at that time --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the very bottom of the page; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed. We can see from the sixth page, or the next page, at the top, that one copy is delivered to the TO brigade in Plaski. So SAO Krajina unit. Normally we would have been able to identify the addressees from the first page, but I see that not everything is legible on the first page. So this is a -- this copy is actually a copy that was received by the TO brigade Plaski. There will also be a copy of this order, at least a copy -- one copy at the unit that issued the order. We have the receive -- we have a receiver's copy. Okay. We can then go to paragraphs 4 and 5, so headings 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which pages would those be on?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: That's page 2 of 6. So again we can stay with the headings 4 and 5 first. In heading 4, again the commander Cedomir Bulat issues his order, a general order, that he has -- his -- units under his command will attack in the direction as specified. It also mentions the municipality of Saborsko. And then in paragraph 5, heading 5, the commander details the order for the subordinate units, and he -- for example, he uses different heading numbers, like 6 for the TO squad. And in 5 you could see TO Plaski.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, could that receive a number and be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 51, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next -- I'm reminded by my colleague that we've reached the hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it convenient for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: It certainly is. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. That being the case, then -- just one point that I would like to raise with the parties. I seem to remember that at the previous hearing we talked about agreed facts that were supposed to be cleaned up and not refiled but just corrected on the record on the documents that are already there. I know it's Mr. Whiting who was dealing with that. Is there any progress report we can get on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's been done, Your Honour. We have an agreement on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. No, we have not done it on the record, and I can do that, if you want. I can tell you what the changes to the question that the Court raised, what the -- the change to the -- the correction. I can do that on the record, if the Court wishes.

utterances.text: If you could do that, and I see you looking at a piece of paper. If you do have it in writing it would be nice, maybe once you have agreed on its contents with Mr. Milovancevic, just to hand it up, please.

In the last -- the last sentence, where the Court pointed out there was an obvious error, it should read as follows: "Finally, the declaration stated that if Yugoslavia remained to be a federation, the Serbs in Croatia would demand cultural autonomy, but if Yugoslavia became a confederation -" and that's the change - "they had the right to political and territorial autonomy."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You confirm, Mr. Milovancevic? In fact, I think that's what you said on that day. If you could just say what --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely correct, Your Honour. Your observation was absolutely right. It was a technical error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. There was a second point, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The second point, I think we agreed when it was first raised. It had to do with the -- when Croatia and Slovenia declared independence. And we agreed on that on the record when it was first raised. So I think that one has been resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I wasn't -- I was amiss on that one. That's the hour. The matter then stands adjourned to tomorrow at 9.00. May the Court adjourn.
